questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I already knew quite a bit of japanese and wanted to take it further and living in Japan made that possible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Best thing i've done.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy to find if you havent prepared beforehand.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received an orientation package but that was quite a bit after I arrived so I didnt really receive much help. I had to figure obligatory insurance, residence etc. out myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy i just searched for short term accomodation Tokyo. I found a site called Hmlett within 2-3 days of mailing them I already had my contract up. I could even sign it all before I left for Japan making it very easy upon my arrival. I greatly recommend them, thought they are quite expensive most of their properties are 9k dkk + per month.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Research the train lines near your accomodation and which train lines run near your university. For waseda any place near a tozai line station is very good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Waseda has a gambling esque roulette system where you have multiple sign up round and you're not guaranteed to get your course so you might find yourself in the last round of registration not having what you need and scrambling to get something that can give you credit at KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really anything I went to them and asked if they could do something they just said to sign up for as much as possible that might give me credit but they couldnt guarantee anything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and got what I wanted, but I know many that didnt get what they needed and thus couldnt fulfill requirements from their home unis.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the first registration round sign up for anything and everything that might be able to give credits you can always drop later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy and not very challenging mostly a lot of filler work that just took time.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A lot of the courses (even advanced ones) felt like entry level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more showing up to classes and taking attendance - show up and do your work it mostly doesnt matter how well you do it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Japanese & Northeast Asian Security 51
Public Choice Theory and Japense Politics
Financial Management 51
Comprehensive Japanese 3
Kanji 3

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i dont really have anything I recommend. If you like international relations take the security course very good professor and interesting perspective into how they view security policies in the east. If you like political science and also enjoy discrete math/logic public choice theory is fantastic and a very fun professor.  I dont recommend any of japanese (CJL) courses their teaching style is quite bad and especially the kanji courses have insane levels of homework compared to the credits you get from the class so avoid that if you can. Comprehensive 3 also has a lot more homework than the other levels.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: drinking and eating out every night also taxis.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Drinking, food and taxis are very cheap, but beware if you do it every night you will spend a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The club and circle activities were the best part.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many types of sport and leisure activities like talking, painting etc theres basically a club for every hobby.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend the Paddy Fielders club (shortly called Paddy) a club where international students and japanese students meet up twice a week for 2ish hours and talk about anything they want. Great way to meet new people and theres also some language practive some times, but you can refrain if you do not want to. They also hold dinners and other events monthly which are really fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend taking a trip out to the middle of nowhere and talk to locals and just take it in. Hokkaido and Aomori are also great.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since I knew a lot about it beforehand - but I find the danish and japanese mindset is quite similar so its not too bad.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They're reserved in the beginning but quickly open up.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Japanese people are very indirect they wont say what they think and will be a bit two faced at times its not malicious they're just not well used to being direct so the danish of communicating is hard for them and vice versa.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hospitality and cleanliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join a club or activity to make friends both local and other exchange students
Go out as much as possible! your time is short make the most of it, it'll be over before you know it.
Focus less on studying and more on the experience itself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think ive said it all.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know so many great people who ill hopefully know for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I got a 43 degree fever and had to go the hospital, but the japanese emergency operators were horrible and i had to call 8 hospitals in my delirious state for help and they all said no, it took around 1h on the phone before they sent and ambulance. After a few hours they threw me out on the street again in bad clothes barely any phone charge still sick having to find my way home. If you get sick dont wait until the last moment or the weekend - their healthcare basically stops on the weekends so its hard to get help.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
